Replacing a removed direct input-output edge with a skip restores connectivity, giving a large gain.
Removing a strong 3x3 conv on the direct edge costs more than removing a 1x1 conv.
With edge 0 removed, node 1 is disconnected so upgrading edge 4 yields almost no gain.
A pooling direct edge reduces the benefit of upgrading edge 5 to 3x3 conv.
A pooling direct edge reduces the benefit of upgrading edge 4 to 3x3 conv.
Replacing a 3x3 conv with pooling loses capacity, whereas replacing weaker ops is roughly neutral or positive.
Replacing a 3x3 conv with a skip removes learned capacity, unlike replacing none or 1x1 conv.
Deleting a 3x3 conv on edge 0 costs far more than deleting a 1x1 conv, skip or pool.
Swapping a 3x3 conv for a skip on the direct edge hurts, whereas swapping a 1x1 conv helps.

raw:
These hypotheses rest on the 100 measurements above. In each case the condition's effect has the same sign on all three datasets and is large.

1. Edge 0 → nor_conv_3x3 gains less when edge 3 is avg_pool_3x3 (+1.8/+1.2/+1.9 against about +3.3/+4.7/+8.6 otherwise).
2. Edge 3 → skip_connect gains more when edge 3 was none (+2.9/+6.5/+13.8 against about +1.9/+2.8/+5.0 on conv1x1).
3. Edge 3 → none hurts more when edge 3 was nor_conv_3x3 (-3.8/-6.5/-17.5 against -1.0/-3.7/-8.8 on conv1x1).
4. Edge 4 → nor_conv_3x3 gains less when edge 0 is none (+0.6/-0.4/+0.8 against about +2.9/+5.1/+8.8).
5. Edge 5 → nor_conv_3x3 gains less when edge 3 is avg_pool_3x3 (+1.3/+0.8/+3.1 against +2.9/+4.0/+8.1).
6. Edge 4 → nor_conv_3x3 gains less when edge 3 is avg_pool_3x3 (+0.8/+1.7/+1.4).
7. Edge 2 → avg_pool_3x3 is worse when edge 2 was nor_conv_3x3 (-2.5/-2.7/-6.2 against a small positive effect on the other parents).
8. Edge 5 → skip_connect is worse when edge 5 was nor_conv_3x3 (-2.7/-4.5/-8.8 against about 0 on conv1x1).
9. Edge 0 → none is worse when edge 0 was nor_conv_3x3 (-4.0/-5.5/-10.2 against -0.7/-0.8/-1.6 on conv1x1).
10. Edge 3 → skip_connect is worse when edge 3 was nor_conv_3x3 (-1.0/0.0/-3.7 against +1.9/+2.8/+5.0 on conv1x1).
